questions.q: In the Meridian Freight scenario, why is the monthly ERP server patching cycle implemented as a Standard change?
options: Because it's the same action, performed the same way, on a known schedule, already reviewed once — exactly what a Change Template pre-authorizes
Because it never affects any Configuration Item
Because finance and operations requested it directly
Because it only happens during emergencies
questions.explain: A repeatable, pre-approved action is the defining case for a Standard change built from a Change Template, per Lesson 10.

questions.q: Why does the scenario implement risk as a rules-based lookup rather than open-ended weighted scoring?
options: Because one fact dominates: any change touching the production database (ERP-PROD-DB01) should be High risk, full stop, regardless of other answers
Because rules-based lookups are the only method ServiceNow supports
Because weighted scoring cannot be built on the change_request table
Because the scenario has no Normal changes at all
questions.explain: When one condition should unambiguously force the outcome, a rules-based lookup is the more reliable implementation choice, per Lesson 11.

questions.q: In the two-stage approval flow built for this scenario, which changes correctly pick up the second (CAB) stage?
options: Every single change submitted, with no exceptions
Only Emergency changes
Changes where risk comes back Medium or High after manager approval resolves — such as any change touching the production database
Only changes submitted by the operations team
questions.explain: The If condition after Stage 1 checks the calculated risk field; Medium or High risk adds the CAB-approval stage, per Lesson 12's pattern.

questions.q: What did Conflict Detection catch in the scenario involving the index change and the storage firmware update?
options: That two changes were submitted by the same requester
That both changes affected the same Configuration Item (ERP-PROD-DB01) with overlapping scheduled windows
That the index change had no backout plan
That the firmware update was missing a risk assessment entirely
questions.explain: Conflict Detection flags overlapping scheduled windows on the same CI automatically, surfacing the collision before the CAB meets, per Lesson 13.

questions.q: How did the CAB resolve the flagged conflict in the scenario, rather than ignoring it?
options: By approving both changes to run concurrently with no changes
By rescheduling the index change to the following Saturday instead of letting both changes run concurrently against the same production database
By deleting the firmware update change record
By reclassifying the index change as a Standard change
questions.explain: A well-implemented CAB process requires the board to explicitly resolve a flagged conflict, here by rescheduling one of the two changes.
